$comment: HAND-WRITTEN, unlike analysis/schema.json, narrative_schema.json and shipped_schema.json, which are generated because a server and a phone both have to agree with them. This document never leaves the machine: it becomes lines in a rules file the author edits and keeps, so there is one consumer and one definition, and a generator would be ceremony around a single output.
title: ProposedRules

rules.description: One proposed rule per recurring failure, at most. Fewer is fine and zero is a real answer.

rule.description: The line to put in the rules file, written as an instruction to the agent. Imperative, specific, and useless if it is vague: 'be careful with the database' stops nothing. (max 220 chars)

because.description: Why it is there, in one sentence, naming the failure and how many sittings hit it. This is the half that survives a year. (max 200 chars)

candidate.description: Which numbered candidate from the input this rule is for. A rule for a candidate you were not shown is a rule about a failure that never happened.

confidence.description: certain: the error states the fix. likely: the fix follows from the error. guess: you are inferring, and the author should check before keeping it.
